# Reviewer/325 — round 1

Head: `9a77968f9528cd7cd099e4fcb5693e745b0f1a2d`.

**Verdict: PASS WITH NOTES.** No code correctness blocker. Independent alarm/cooldown/launch-env mutations are killed; the restored 11-daemon/22-spawn baseline and version probe are green.

The mass-death count is the death sweep's successfully committed retirements, not all tombstones. The reaper lists only live rows and skips a row already tombstoned by normal close, so closing six completed review seats through `pij close` does not itself trigger the alarm. Killing six hosts/panes without first recording their close does count as observed deaths, irrespective of whether the operator intended that shutdown; a PA notice to inspect the shared cause is appropriate. Existing reaper eligibility and its conservative process/pane guards are unchanged.

The within-process boundaries are consistent: exactly five in one sweep triggers; fewer can accumulate until ten are within the rolling window; age exactly 60 seconds is excluded; the quiet period is shorter-than-60 seconds, so a due alarm can fire at the exact boundary if qualifying deaths remain. Empty sweeps prune the window and can deliver a deferred threshold after the quiet period. Counting uses committed rows, not dry-run candidates or already-retired seats.

**N325-1 (known limit, wording owed):** both the rolling window and `last_alarm_at` are process-local. Restart can miss a storm split across two daemon lifetimes, and can permit two alarms less than 60 seconds apart across a restart. “At most one per 60 seconds” is guaranteed only within one daemon process, not across restarts. The coder corrected the PR body after review feedback. The same qualification is still owed in the MassDeath source comment, API docs and D-F271b-1 ledger text; no durable-state mechanism is requested as part of this small fix.

Spawn and revive converge at `launch_seat_locked` -> `build_spawn_plan`, where the Copilot-only environment assignment is placed before the executable, including model/provider wiring, resume and executable overrides. The launch wrapper preserves discrete argv. `installedVersion()` independently forces both offline and auto-update-off, overriding an inherited `COPILOT_AUTO_UPDATE=true`.

**N325-2 (known limit, wording owed):** F212/F261 recovery queues Copilot's `restart` control; it is not a new pij SpawnPlan and does not retrofit the environment of an existing or adopted process. All pij-built new spawn/revive launches receive the variable, but already-running/adopted seats require a full pij relaunch to receive it. Current-build CLI documentation confirms the env disables auto-update and startup plugin updates; it does not document `/restart` environment inheritance. No live restart canary is claimed. The coder added this limit to the PR body; the native-extension docs still need the same scope.

The installed-binary contract-pass limitation is already stated: this flag does not prevent manual replacement of the installed binary or independently prove that every installed version was checked. The launch-time kill deny is explicitly out of scope. No kill-by-pattern command was executed for this review.

The alarm changes notification behavior, not retirement eligibility. Its threshold/window decide notification admission; the cooldown limits repeat wakes. It never kills or revives a seat. Alarm selection failures and failed PA deliveries are recorded/logged; delivery is best-effort to live PAs, using the existing watchdog wake path.

Cost: no new poll/timer or daemon launch site. The existing five-second sweep adds a short mutex-protected deque update, `O(recent + retired)` pruning/appending, including pruning on empty sweeps while the deque is nonempty. On an alarm it adds a live-seat/role lookup, one existing delivery per PA, and one spine event. The per-process limit is one alarm per minute; restart resets that limit. “Zero work when nothing died” should mean the empty-window case, not a nonempty recent window. Performance owns live measurements.

## Validation

Initial and final freeze rechecks briefly reported GitHub's UNKNOWN, then `just pr-freeze 325` returned exit 0, FINAL/CLEAN at the requested head, latest five checks green, no migration. Main advanced to schema 50 during review; this head remains 49 but adds no migration and merges cleanly.

Exact-head CI run `44923632187`, successful rust-test job `136904824249`, upload-log-selected artifact `14715036912`: 2,821 JUnit cases, no failures. The mass-death thresholds, five-retirement PA wake, and Copilot-only environment tests are present and passed.

Independent controls add exact-window/restart cases and a real-store six-tombstone normal-close fixture in an owned archive. `just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --lib -- death_sweep a_sweep_retiring_five reviewer_325 --nocapture --then test -p pij-harnesses spawn:: -- --nocapture`: exit 0, 11 daemon and 22 spawn tests passed. The close fixture checks the tombstoned end state directly, paired with source tracing of the normal close path; it is not a live `pij close` call.

A private fake executable independently verified `installedVersion()` overrides inherited auto-update=true and keeps offline=true; no installed Copilot binary or live seat was launched by that probe.

Independent M1 (alarm admission disabled): `just shared-build -- test -p pij-daemon --lib -- mass_death a_sweep_retiring_five reviewer_325 --nocapture` returned exit 101, with three intended assertion failures (five-death threshold, exact-window threshold, and the real-store `death.mass` event). The normally closed-seat control still passed. Compilation succeeded.

Independent M2 (quiet-minute guard disabled): the two threshold/restart-control tests returned exit 101 on their cooldown assertions. Independent M6 (Copilot env omitted): the dedicated spawn test returned exit 101 on its environment-placement assertion. Both compiled successfully. Removing the version helper's env override was also caught by the private fake CLI, which exited 42 when it received inherited auto-update=true; Node surfaced that error and exited 1.

Production spawn/version helper files are restored byte-for-byte; death-sweep and reaper files differ only by the retained reviewer tests. The restored command returned exit 0: 11 daemon and 22 spawn tests passed, followed by the successful restored version-env probe. Author receipts M1-M6 in PR comment `7065301165` were inspected separately, not treated as reviewer reruns of M3-M5. Local boot is dependency-limited under C25; all cargo uses shared-build, the resolved shared target, niceness 19 and four jobs.

`harness checks --quick --json`: exit 1 due to absent worktree dependencies and incompatible ambient Biome; native Copilot contracts, SDK, and skill checks passed. No local full-gate success is claimed and no shared dependencies were linked or installed.

Receipts retained: baseline/restored logs, M1/M2/M6 logs, version-env failure/restoration logs and fake-CLI source, reviewer test patch, mutation patches, local-gate envelope and exact-head JUnit archive. The owned temporary source archive and executable fixture are removed after verification.

**Notes owed:** qualify the MassDeath source comment, API docs and D-F271b-1 text to cover both restart-reset behaviors; qualify native-extension docs to new pij spawn/revive rather than existing/adopted `/restart` seats. These limitations are now stated in the PR body and do not require new alarm persistence or launch-deny machinery.

**Harness lesson:** state the scope of in-memory safety counters explicitly and test restart boundaries; argv environment proof is not proof that an existing process was retrofitted.
